title: Shanti and Anushasana: Bhishma's teachings from the bed of arrows (selections)
hook: the old man who could choose the hour of his death waits for the sun to turn, then asks Krishna for leave to go
carry: the arrows fall from him one by one

segments.voice: Yesterday, in Gautami's story, the chain of blame ran back through the snake, Death and Time. Your line was let it go.

Bhishma carries an unusual gift. Long ago, his father blessed him so that death would come only when he chose it. So he has been lying on the arrows, teaching, and waiting for a particular turning of the year: the time when the sun begins its northward course, called uttarayana, which the tradition holds as an auspicious time to die. He sent Yudhishthira back to the city to rule. Now the season has turned, and Yudhishthira returns to the field with fire, garlands and everything needed for the last rites.
screen: `DEATH ONLY WHEN HE CHOOSES.` → `WAITING FOR THE SUN TO TURN.` → `YUDHISHTHIRA RETURNS.`

segments.voice: Bhishma opens his eyes and sees them all around him: Yudhishthira and his brothers, Dhritarashtra, Gandhari, Kunti, Krishna. The time has come, he says. He tells Dhritarashtra, the blind king whose sons are gone, not to grieve, and to treat the Pandavas as his own. Then he turns to Krishna and asks for leave to go. A man who can choose his own death still asks permission to take it. Krishna gives it. And then Bhishma does something the text describes almost like a meditation. He draws his life breath inward, part by part. As it withdraws from each limb, the story says, the arrows in that part fall away and the wound closes. Limb by limb, the bed of arrows lets him go. At last the breath leaves through the crown of his head, rising like a great light into the sky. His family builds the pyre and performs the rites, then goes down to the Ganga to offer water. The river goddess herself rises from it, weeping. Bhishma was her son, and she grieves that he fell to Shikhandi. Krishna comforts her: it was Arjuna who brought him down, with Shikhandi only standing in front, and her son has gone to the heavens. Don't grieve. So the teaching from the bed of arrows ends without a speech: a man finishing his work, asking leave, and going when it's time, while the arrows fall from him one by one.
screen: `"THE TIME HAS COME"` · `HE ASKS KRISHNA FOR LEAVE` · `THE ARROWS FALL AWAY` · then, large: `GANGA WEEPS FOR HER SON`

segments.voice: Let your body be heavy and supported, and with each slow out-breath let one part soften and let go: your feet, your legs, your belly, your shoulders, your face. Take your time, part by part, the way the arrows fell away; there's nothing to finish right now. If you pray, you can rest in your prayer as you let go.
uttarayana. The sun's northward course: the season Bhishma waited for, when he could finally let go and die.
Your line: the arrows fall from him one by one. Tomorrow, a new book opens: Ashvamedhika. Day eight hundred sixty-six, done.

howItsDone: Bhishma's death at uttarayana is remembered in Hindu tradition, and some communities observe a day in his memory, Bhishma Ashtami, with water offerings in his name.

what a scholar hears: the death is told as a yogic withdrawal, and the arrows falling away turn the bed of arrows into a release.

chat.says: Why did Bhishma wait on the arrows instead of dying right away?
options: He could choose his time, and he waited for the sun's northward turn.
Krishna wouldn't allow him to die until every last battle was over.
He was waiting for Arjuna to come back and pull out every arrow.
chat.meaning: Bhishma's father blessed him to die only when he chose. He waited for uttarayana, which tradition holds as an auspicious time.

uttarayana.meaning: the sun's northward course, an auspicious season

Ganga.meaning: the sacred river, and the goddess who was Bhishma's mother

Shikhandi.meaning: the warrior Arjuna fought behind to bring Bhishma down

Dhritarashtra.meaning: the blind Kuru king, father of Duryodhana

recall: the boy who went to Death's house unafraid
